ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Albert Einstein

code.originalText: Four-week follow-up: CT angiography results, vascular surgery consultation, and a shared decision about repair thresholds

text.paragraph: Four-week follow-up: CT angiography results and vascular surgery consultation the same day. [S]

Mr. Einstein is a 70-year-old man with a 5.0 cm infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm by duplex ultrasound, found and wrapped at a prior exploratory laparotomy, who returns four weeks after his first visit for the CT angiography results and is seen by vascular surgery on the same day. He has had no abdominal, back, or flank pain, fainting, or leg symptoms. He stopped smoking on his quit date a week after the first visit and has had no tobacco for three weeks. He wears the 14 mg patch daily and uses three or four lozenges a day, and he holds an empty, unlit pipe while he works, which he finds helps. He started losartan 50 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg four weeks ago without side effects; his home blood pressure readings average 134/80. The CT angiography two weeks ago showed a 5.2 cm fusiform infrarenal aneurysm with a 2.2 cm neck, calcified atheroma of the aorta and iliac arteries, thickening along the front of the aneurysm from the old wrapping, and no fluid around the aorta. [S]

list.item:
Infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm under surveillance (I71.43). Asymptomatic aneurysm of 5.0 cm by ultrasound and 5.2 cm by CT outer-wall measurement, below the 5.5 cm threshold for elective repair in men. The old wrapping does not change the thresholds or the surveillance plan. A shared decision was made with vascular surgery and recorded: surveillance by duplex ultrasound every six months, with elective repair advised at 5.5 cm, growth of 0.5 cm or more in six months, or symptoms, and endovascular repair favored on this anatomy. His preferences are recorded in the consultation. [S]
Duplex ultrasound every six months, using ultrasound consistently for comparison.
Carry the aneurysm wallet card; emergency plan reviewed.

Atherosclerosis of the abdominal aorta (I70.0). Calcified atheroma on CT angiography, which supports a high-intensity statin and low-dose aspirin. [S]
Start aspirin 81 mg daily with food, as vascular surgery advises.
Continue atorvastatin 40 mg.

Essential hypertension (I10). Above the 130/80 target at the clinic and at home on amlodipine 5 mg and losartan 50 mg; potassium 4.6 and creatinine 1.08 after four weeks of losartan. [S]
Increase losartan to 100 mg daily.
Metabolic panel and home readings before the three-month visit.

Nicotine dependence, pipe tobacco (F17.290). Abstinent for three weeks on nicotine replacement. [S]
Continue the 14 mg patch and lozenges; quitline support offered.
